verdict.rationale: Docs show each skill's SKILL.md must declare a `description`, and the plugin/skill creation flow explicitly asks 'what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only' (codex-plugins-docs-13, codex-plugins-docs-7), which directly supports predictable documentation of scope and activation. However, community commentary voices skepticism about reliability of this mechanism ('you just selectively append more text to prompt and pray' — codex-plugins-comm-2), suggesting activation prediction isn't always crisp in practice, and there's no independent audit confirming descriptions reliably prevent surprise behavior across skills. Missing for 10: independent verification/testing that activation triggers behave as documented, examples of well-written vs. ambiguous SKILL.md descriptions, and resolution of the community concern about unpredictable triggering.
